Title: PGDip in Artificial Intelligence in Education (entry in January 2027) | Oxford University
# PGDip in Artificial Intelligence in Education (entry in January 2027). For professionals working in education, policy and technology interested in developing competency as research-informed leaders in the field. Upcoming application deadline for 2026-27 entry:. Final application deadline for entry in January 2027. All applications received by the deadline shown above will be considered only for entry in the 2026-27 academic year, starting in January 2027. Applications for entry in the 2027-28 academic year (starting in Autumn 2027) are expected to open later in November and you should consult the separate course page for further details. The course information on this page applies only for applications for entry in the 2026-27 academic year (starting in January 2027). Course information for entry in the 2027-28 academic year, including application deadlines, is available on a separate course page. The PGDip Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Education responds to the global need for a credible and prestigious degree qualification designed to provide professionals across education, policy, and the technology industry with critical literacy, research training, and applied expertise to lead AI in education. This interdisciplinary course draws on the expertise of Computer Scientists, Engineers and Data Scientists from across the University of Oxford to support the core teaching team in the Department of Education. Drawing on Oxford’s expertise in research, pedagogy, and policy engagement, this course will empower you to set the global standard for rigorous, ethical, and considered practice in AI and education. In addition, as a result of enrolling in this course, you will benefit from:. Work on your independent study will begin with discussions with your supervisor at the start of the course, and will be your sole focus of the third term and the long vacation. Prior to the formal start of the course, you will attend a one-week residential module in the Department of Education in Oxford. The week will help to prepare you for the course by introducing key themes around research and evidence in AI in education, exploring the core principles of the course, introducing you to the University’s IT and library systems, and providing guidance on engaging with research literature and writing for an academic audience.
